lines: Title: Endomorphism Ring of Abelian Group is Ring with Unity
Let $\struct {\map {\mathrm {End} } G, \oplus, \circ}$ be its [[Definition:Endomorphism Ring of Abelian Group|endomorphism ring]].
Then $\struct {\map {\mathrm {End} } G, \oplus, \circ}$ is a [[Definition:Ring with Unity|ring]] with [[Definition:Unity of Ring|unity]] $I_G$, where:
:$\oplus$ is the [[Definition:Pointwise Operation|pointwise operation on $\map {\mathrm {End} } G$ induced by $+$]].
In the below, $f, g , h \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G$.
As $f, g, h$ are [[Definition:Group Endomorphism|(group) endomorphisms]], it follows {{afortiori}} that they are also [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|(group) homomorphisms]].
Recall that $f \oplus g$ is the [[Definition:Pointwise Operation|pointwise operation]] on $f$ and $g$ [[Definition:Pointwise Operation|induced by $+$]].
We are [[Definition:Given|given]] that $\struct {G, +}$ is an [[Definition:Abelian Group|abelian group]].
By [[Homomorphism on Induced Structure to Commutative Semigroup]], $f \oplus g$ is a [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] from $\struct {G, +}$ into $\struct {G, +}$.
So, by definition, $f \oplus g$ is an [[Definition:Group Endomorphism|endomorphism]] on $\struct {G, +}$.
Now, taking the [[Axiom:Ring Axioms|ring axioms]] in turn:
We have that $f \oplus g$ is an [[Definition:Group Endomorphism|endomorphism]] on $\struct {G, +}$.
:$\forall f, g \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G: f \oplus g \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G$
Hence, by definition, $\struct {\map {\mathrm {End} } G, \oplus}$ is [[Definition:Closed Algebraic Structure|closed]].
By [[Homomorphism on Induced Structure to Commutative Semigroup]] again, we have:
:$\forall f, g, h \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G: \paren {f \oplus g} \oplus h = f \oplus \paren {g \oplus h}$
By [[Homomorphism on Induced Structure to Commutative Semigroup]] again, we have:
We are [[Definition:Given|given]] that $I_G$ is the [[Definition:Identity Mapping|identity mapping]] on $G$.
By [[Identity Mapping is Ring Automorphism]], $I_G$ is an [[Definition:Ring Automorphism|automorphism]] on $G$.
Follows from [[Pointwise Inverse in Induced Structure]].
By [[Composite of Homomorphisms is Homomorphism]], for any [[Definition:Homomorphism|homomorphisms]] $f$ and $g$, $f \circ g$ is also a [[Definition:Homomorphism|homomorphism]].

By [[Composite of Endomorphisms is Endomorphism]], if $f$ and $g$ are [[Definition:Endomorphism|endomorphisms]], then the [[Definition:Composition of Mappings|composite]] of $f$ and $g$ is also an [[Definition:Endomorphism|endomorphism]]
:$\forall f, g \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G: f \circ g \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G$
From [[Structure Induced by Associative Operation is Associative]] we have that:
:$\forall f, g, h \in \map {\mathrm {End} } G: \paren{f \circ g} \circ h = f \circ \paren{g \circ h}$
By [[Composition of Mappings is Left Distributive over Homomorphism of Pointwise Operation]]:
By [[Composition of Mappings is Right Distributive over Pointwise Operation]]:

So it follows from definition of [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributive]] that [[Definition:Composition of Mappings|composition of mappings]] is [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributive]] over [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] of the [[Definition:Pointwise Operation|pointwise operation]] $\oplus$.

As $f, g, h$ are [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|endomorphisms]], it follows that [[Definition:Composition of Mappings|composition of mappings]] is [[Definition:Distributive Operation|distributive]] over [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|endomorphism]] of $\oplus$.
Hence $\struct {\map {\mathrm {End} } G, \oplus, \circ}$ is a [[Definition:Ring with Unity|ring]] with [[Definition:Unity of Ring|unity]] $I_G$.
